notes: The diagnostic owns nonpaged system memory and copies its actual PFN identities from a temporary MDL. It frees that input descriptor before accessing the pages through independently created mappings. It does not borrow a parent system mapping.

An unaligned fill checks every source byte including guards, followed by a page-crossing read/write round trip. Unmap points all 5063 addresses to the same real owned dummy page; reads and writes across adjacent aliases are independently checked against the original dummy memory.

This is real kernel mapping evidence, not VidMm allocation or aperture-DDI acceptance. The driver deliberately rejects startup, resulting in Code 43 for the laboratory node. The original display remains healthy and removal succeeds.

The debugger log preserves a symbol-path setup typo: semicolon-separated commands were interpreted as path entries. The path was corrected and the guest resumed before installation; this did not modify guest code or the diagnostic.
No fabricated CPU bus address, OS pointer patch, synthetic Windows fence, NPU execution, desktop composition or Tahoma measurement was used.
